neighbours.label: field-geology description of where rock beds appear or how they lie: 'exposed' (in cliffs, at the mouth of a gorge), 'strike', outcrops
fire: Thick beds of red sandstone are exposed along the north bank of the river.
At low tide, the old lava flows are exposed on the foreshore below the village.
The coal seams are well exposed in the railway cutting east of the station.
The shale layers strike north-east and dip gently towards the sea.
Ancient gneiss is exposed in the walls of the canyon for several miles.
Further upstream, the conglomerate is exposed in a small quarry.
The limestone outcrop on the hillside shows clear fossil corals.
Where the road climbs the ridge, folded slates are exposed in the bank.
quiet: Thick beds of red sandstone formed in a hot desert millions of years ago.
The old lava flows cooled quickly and cracked into tall columns.
The coal seams were mined for two centuries before the pits closed.
The shale contains tiny fossils of ancient plankton.
Ancient gneiss forms the oldest part of the continental crust.
The children were exposed to cold rain on the long walk home.
The newspaper story exposed a scandal at the town hall.
Where the road climbs the ridge, the view over the valley is wide.

notes: card: ' exposed' x5 of the top 32 (granodiorite exposed near the coast, beds exposed in the channel), plus ' strike', ' Shield', ' known'. Probes: geology 'exposed in the cliffs' 0.40, 'beds strike north' 0.40, 'outcrops' 0.35; non-geology 'exposed to fumes' 0.003, 'scandal exposed' 0.008. Near misses: geology prose without exposure/attitude terms, and 'exposed' in other senses.
